text: In what appears to be the most convincing performance of Drake Maye's season thus far, the Patriots absolutely demolished the Raiders 45-17 at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, with the young quarterback accounting for five total touchdowns despite being without his top receiver and operating behind an offensive line missing starting left tackle Will Campbell. The dominant victory is particularly noteworthy given that New England was also down both starting cornerbacks, yet still managed to cruise to a wire-to-wire victory that has apparently helped restore some of the confidence and deep-ball accuracy that had been missing during Maye's slower start to the year. The good news came with a significant price, however: running back TreVeyon Henderson suffered an ankle injury during the game, while Campbell departed with what NFL Network sources believe to be a knee sprain, adding to what's already been a brutal injury situation for the Patriots heading into the weeks ahead. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's health situation and the impressive Week 5 performance at Monday's press conference, while film review revealed one of Maye's cleanest outings against a Raiders defense that couldn't keep pace with New England's offensive firepower.
